title: Why Units Die in the Layer After a Frozen Random Encoder, and What the Number of Live Units Measures
abstract: arXiv:2611.29752v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reinforcement-learning agents can learn Atari games through a convolutional encoder whose random weights are never trained. They reach expert play in Pong and, without random action repeats, in Breakout, but training takes far longer and few ReLU units in the layer after the encoder stay alive. A dead unit outputs zero for every input and cannot learn. In earlier work we took the number of live units to measure the game's complexity. Here we ask why units die and correct that conclusion. We find that more units die as the layer's inputs lie farther from zero relative to how much they vary. We call this ratio the offset. Earlier work showed this in sparse autoencoders at the start of training. We saw it after training in agents, image classifiers, a reservoir computer and sparse autoencoders on GPT-2. A random encoder leaves the offset of its input roughly unchanged, and a formula predicted its median offset within 25 percent in all 44

translated_title: 为什么单元会在冻结随机编码器之后的层中死亡，以及存活单元数量究竟衡量了什么
translated_abstract: 强化学习智能体可以通过一个权重从不被训练的卷积随机编码器来学习雅达利游戏。它们在《乓》中达到了专家水平，在不使用随机动作重复的情况下也能在《打砖块》中达到专家水平，但训练耗时要长得多，且编码器之后那一层中只有少数ReLU单元保持存活。死亡单元对每个输入都输出零，因而无法学习。在早期工作中，我们将存活单元的数量作为衡量游戏复杂度的指标。本文中我们探究单元为何死亡，并纠正了那一结论。我们发现，当该层的输入相对于其变化幅度而言离零越远时，死亡的单元就越多。我们将这一比值称为偏移量。早期工作已在训练开始时的稀疏自编码器中展示了这一现象；而我们在训练后的强化学习智能体、图像分类器、储备池计算机以及GPT-2上的稀疏自编码器中都观察到了这一现象。随机编码器会使其输入的偏移量大致保持不变，且一个公式在全部44个案例中将其中位偏移量的预测误差控制在25%以内。
tldr: 本文揭示编码器后层单元死亡的原因是输入的偏移量（均值相对于变化幅度的比值）过大，从而纠正了此前“存活单元数量可衡量游戏复杂度”的结论。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that units die in the layer after a frozen random encoder because of large input offsets (the mean relative to variability), correcting the earlier conclusion that the number of live units measures game complexity.
